summary: The GRASP model exhibits expected stereo-blindness but fails SMILES invariance checks, suggesting sensitivity to input string features rather than pure graph topology. Pretrained activations show layer-dependent scaling, while random-init activations remain constant at high magnitude. Input tokens have ambiguity regarding aromaticity for 25% of atoms.

claims.claim: The model is sensitive to SMILES permutation (not purely topological invariant).
claims.test: SMARTS: c1ccccc1; Compare canonical vs random SMILES for 10 molecules. Prediction: Distance ~0 if topological invariant.
claims.prediction: Distance should be ~0 (float16 noise level). Observed 0.534 implies string-based features or non-canonical graph construction affect embeddings.

claims.claim: The model ignores stereochemistry (enantiomers treated as identical).
claims.test: SMARTS: C[C@H](N)O vs C[C@@H](N)O; Compare layer-12 CLS vectors.
claims.prediction: Distance should be 0 if stereo-blind. Observed 0 confirms model lacks chiral input features (e.g., no chirality flag in atom tokens).

claims.claim: Pretrained model learns layer-dependent activation scaling, unlike random-init which maintains constant high magnitude.
claims.test: Compare per-layer norms for pretrained vs random on cached 'atoms' set.
claims.prediction: Pretrained norms should vary by layer; Random should be constant (if initialized with LayerNorm). Observed variation confirms pretraining adjusts activation scales.

claims.claim: Input tokenization has ambiguity regarding aromaticity for 25% of atoms.
claims.test: SMARTS: c1ccccc1 (aromatic) vs C1CCCCC1 (aliphatic); Check 'aromatic' column for each atom.
claims.prediction: Tokens should be distinct if aromaticity is encoded. Observed mixing implies some tokens (e.g., Carbon) can represent both contexts, forcing model to learn from neighbors.

claims.claim: Pretrained CLS representation spans more dimensions than random noise.
claims.test: Compute participation ratio of CLS covariance for 'mols' set.
claims.prediction: Pretrained rank should be higher than random (noise). Observed 9.9 vs 5.8 confirms pretraining expands representational capacity relevant to chemistry.

trivial_explanations: SMILES invariance failure likely due to input tokenization including string features or non-canonical graph construction, not just atom counts.
Stereo blindness is expected for graph models without explicit chiral inputs (e.g., no @/@@ flags).
Random-init norms are constant because LayerNorm preserves variance during initialization; Pretrained norms vary because learning adjusts scales.
